newsitem.title: USA: Enron says buyback to come from cash flow.
newsitem.headline: Enron says buyback to come from cash flow.

text.p: Enron Oil & Gas Co will finance its five million share buyback from internal cash flow and will not sell assets, a spokesman for the company said.
"We have strong cash flow and relatively low debt, so I do not think we will have any problem funding it," said Hardy Davies, a spokesman for the company.
An existing share buyback of one million shares has already been set.

After the buyback, Enron Oil & Gas shares added 1/2 to 21-5/8, against the background of a flat wider market. The S&P 500 Index was off 0.63 points, or 0.08 percent, at 811.19, while the S&P Oil & Gas Index was unchanged at 71.28 points.
Davis said that Enron Corp, which owns 53 percent of the company, will not be cutting its stake as a result of the buyback.

Earlier this week, Forrest Hoglund, chairman and chief executive officer of Enron Oil & Gas, said that Enron would probably not wish to reduce its stake below 50 percent as it wished to consolidate Enron Oil & Gas in its accounts.
At $21.00 per share the buyback will cost the company in the region of $105 million.
"We are not buying back five million today, it could be over a period of years," said Davies.
"We just think at this price it makes sense for us to buy the shares," he added, stating that Enron Oil & Gas did not have a target price for its stock.
The stock hit a year closing high of 26-1/4 on January 17, but has come off steadily since then.
"Enron Oil & Gas is buying the stock back at a lower premium than the stock has been at for some time and there is little financial impact on the company," said John Parry, analyst at John Herold.
